waste_details.reason_for_no_provision: There is currently no provision for on-site external refuse storage due to the property’s location on a busy main road. The existing lawful use is a dwellinghouse (Use Class C3), and the proposed change of use to a small HMO (Use Class C4) would not result in a material increase in the volume of waste generated. Refuse storage and collection arrangements would therefore remain consistent with the existing arrangements serving the property.

subdivision_of_building: Building is 5 stories including the basement, the basement and ground floor are commercial use and not affected. The affected floors are the 1st, 2nd and 3rd floors which have their own seperate access.
description:
Proposed Development Description (C3 to C4)

The proposal seeks full planning permission for a change of use from a single dwellinghouse (Use Class C3) to a small House in Multiple Occupation (Use Class C4), to be occupied by up to six persons within five bedrooms.

The property is located on Deptford Broadway, within a Major District Centre and an area of excellent public transport accessibility (PTAL 6a). The surrounding context is mixed-use, with commercial premises at ground floor level and residential accommodation above.

Nature of Works

The proposed development involves minimal internal alterations only, with no extensions or external changes to the building fabric. The sole structural alteration is the removal of an existing internal staircase to the rear of the property, enabling that space to function as a utility room. No additional floorspace is created, and the overall residential footprint remains unchanged.

Principle of Change of Use

Although the gross internal area of the original dwelling does not exceed 130 sqm, as referenced in Policy HO8 of the Lewisham Local Plan, the Council’s pre-application advice (PRE/25/141710) confirms that the site is not suitable for family accommodation. This is due to:

The property’s location on a busy main road (Deptford Broadway / A2 corridor), resulting in high levels of noise and reduced air quality;

The absence of private amenity space;

The lack of on-site cycle and refuse storage (typical of upper-floor accommodation above commercial premises);

The highly urban town-centre context.

As confirmed by the Council’s Planning Officer, the loss of the C3 family dwelling is therefore acceptable in this instance, notwithstanding the departure from the 130 sqm threshold, and the principle of a small C4 HMO is supported.

HMO Suitability and Policy Context

The proposal would not result in a harmful overconcentration of HMOs. While the site is within an area identified as having a higher proportion of HMOs, the pre-application response confirms that, given the Major District Centre location, excellent accessibility, and the unsuitability of the unit for family living, this policy conflict is outweighed in this case.

The accommodation will be operated in full compliance with the Lewisham Standards for Licensable HMOs, and a separate HMO licence will be obtained.

Social Value and Community Benefit

The property will be operated in partnership with The 999 Club, a well-established charity based on Deptford Broadway. The accommodation will be used to provide emergency and short-term housing for individuals with a verified local connection to Lewisham, supporting vulnerable residents at risk of homelessness.

This arrangement delivers clear social value, directly responding to local housing need, and aligns with national and local planning objectives relating to inclusive growth, community wellbeing, and the effective use of existing housing stock in accessible locations.
